title: Geometric irreducibility can be checked after an arbitrary field extension
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For a scheme X over k and a field extension k'/k, the lemma shows that geometric irreducibility of X over k is equivalent to geometric irreducibility of the base change over k' (statement lines 1345-1351). One direction is immediate. For the converse the author uses a common extension: given any field extension k''/k, choose a field k''' containing both k' and k''; the base change map from X_{k'''} to X_{k''} is surjective because it is a base change of the surjective morphism between the spectra of the two fields, so irreducibility upstairs implies irreducibility downstairs, and since this holds for every k'' the conclusion follows (proof lines 1353-1363). The claim is H2: a short argument whose only construction is the common extension field, with the surjectivity observation supplying the implication.
